name: Neck Rolls
description: Slowly roll your head in a full circle, 5 times each direction. Keep shoulders relaxed.

name: Shoulder Shrugs
description: Raise both shoulders up to your ears, hold for 3 seconds, then release. Repeat continuously.

name: Standing Calf Raises
description: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Rise up on your toes, hold 2 seconds, lower slowly. Use a wall for balance if needed.

name: Bodyweight Squats
description: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Lower until thighs are parallel to the floor, then stand back up.

name: Wall Push-Ups
description: Place hands on the wall at shoulder height. Lean in and push back. Great upper body activation without getting on the floor.

name: Desk Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Step one foot back into a lunge, lower your back knee toward the floor, and lean forward slightly. Hold each side.

name: March in Place
description: Lift your knees high and pump your arms. Keep a brisk pace — get your heart rate up a little.

name: Torso Twists
description: Sit or stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Rotate your torso left and right, letting your arms swing naturally.

name: Seated Leg Extensions
description: Sit upright in your chair. Extend one leg straight out, hold 3 seconds, lower slowly. Alternate legs.

name: Wrist & Finger Stretches
description: Extend one arm, pull fingers back gently with the other hand. Then press fingers downward. Switch hands. Great for keyboard fatigue.

name: Standing Side Stretch
description: Stand tall, raise one arm overhead and lean to the opposite side. Feel the stretch along your ribs. Switch sides.

name: Stair Climbing
description: Find a staircase and walk up and down continuously. If no stairs, step up and down on a single step.

name: Chair Dips
description: Hands on the edge of a sturdy chair, feet out in front. Lower yourself by bending elbows, then push back up.

name: Eye Rest & Focus
description: Look away from your screen at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Then close your eyes and gently massage your temples.

name: Deep Breathing
description: Inhale slowly for 4 counts, hold for 4, exhale for 6. This activates your parasympathetic nervous system and reduces stress.
